questions.subject: Edo
questions.subtopic: The Edo vowels o and ọ
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish /o/ and /ɔ/ through their spellings in Edo vocabulary.
questions.prompt: A learner files the Edo words ako, gbọ, ukpo and kọ on cards labelled o and ọ. Put the words on the correct cards by inspecting their final vowel letters. Give the IPA symbol for the sound on each card.
questions.answer: o card: ako, ukpo. Sound /o/. ọ card: gbọ, kọ. Sound /ɔ/.
questions.explanation: The final vowel letter in ako and ukpo is undotted o, whereas in gbọ and kọ it is dotted ọ. The dot distinguishes the vowel letter and its associated sound.

markingGuide.description: Group ako and ukpo under o.
Group gbọ and kọ under ọ.

questions.subject: Edo
questions.learningObjective: Locate the spelling kh for /x/ in Edo words and distinguish letters from sounds.
questions.prompt: On a classroom word wall, the target is the Edo consonant /x/. Which of okha, ize, akhe and udu should go on that part of the wall? In each word you select, identify the letters that represent the target consonant.
questions.answer: okha and akhe. In both words, kh represents /x/.
questions.explanation: Each selected word contains the adjacent letters k and h. They spell one consonant in these examples. The other entries do not contain kh.

markingGuide.description: Identify kh as the spelling of one consonant /x/ in the selected words.

questions.subject: Edo
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and spell selected Edo numerals in a written record.
questions.prompt: Two crates in a Benin City school storeroom have word labels. Crate A says Iweva and crate B says Eha-yan-ugie. Write the two quantities in digits. The stock check confirms crate A is correct and crate B actually contains 21 items. Write the corrected Edo word label for crate B.
questions.answer: Crate A: 12. Crate B’s old label: 23. Crate B’s corrected label: Ọkpa-yan-ugie.
questions.explanation: Iweva denotes twelve. In the listed forms for 21 and 23, ọkpa contributes one and eha contributes three to ugie, twenty.

markingGuide.description: Write Ọkpa-yan-ugie for 21, retaining the dotted vowel.

questions.subject: Edo
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a mismatched singular and plural verb pair and restore its counterpart.
questions.prompt: An Edo verb glossary pairs singular and plural forms. A typesetter left these rows: bọ → bọlọ, dẹ → dele, de → dẹlẹ. Identify the two rows that need correction and write their corrected pairs. Explain why the dots matter when checking the pairs.
questions.answer: Correct dẹ → dẹlẹ and de → dele. The bọ → bọlọ row is already correct. The dotted vowel ẹ belongs in dẹ and dẹlẹ, whereas undotted e occurs in de and dele.
questions.explanation: The two plural forms were interchanged. Preserving the vowel letters keeps each singular form matched with its own plural counterpart.

markingGuide.description: Correct dẹ to the pair dẹ → dẹlẹ.
Correct de to the pair de → dele.
Explain that ẹ and e distinguish the paired forms.
